newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Insider trading of bank shares suspected May - FI.
newsitem.headline: Insider trading of bank shares suspected May - FI.

text.p: An investigation into insider trading involving shares of Swedish bank Foreningsbanken AB was triggered by events about five months ago, a spokesman from Sweden's Financial Supervisory Board (FI) said.
Bernt Magnusson, head of securities at FI, told Reuters that the investigation, announced on Thursday, was now in the hands of the state prosecutor's office.
Asked how long the investigation had been going on, Magnusson said "four or five months".
He said the incident involved trade in shares of the bank outside the bank.
He said one of the suspects in the incident worked as an economist for a Swedish union, and stressed he did not work in the bank.
He would not give information about the other two.
"I don't want to comment on that," Magnusson said.
Magnusson said the investigation was now out of FI's hands.
"We have handed it over to the prosecutor and now he has started the investigation," he said.
"The prosecutor will look into this and probably question these three persons and other persons involved. After that he will make a decision if he will go further, to a court."
Foreningsbanken shares were slightly weaker in morning trade, slipping by 20 ore to 27.40 crowns by 0845 GMT.
